abstract: We show that asymptotic safety in functional renormalization group (FRG) gravity arises as a truncation shadow of a well-defined ultraviolet (UV) endpoint functional generated by projection-induced spectral proper-time (SPT) damping in a coherent universality class. Working on bounded-geometry time slabs and within an admissible regulator class, we prove Gaussian-damped shell integrability of the FRG flow and construct a UV endpoint functional \Gamma_\infty in a Banach space of analytic local plus entire form-factor actions. We establish scheme stability of \Gamma_\infty under admissible regulator variations, prove that the linearized RG step at \Gamma_\infty has a finite-dimensional unstable manifold, and demonstrate that fixed points observed in finite truncations are shadows of \Gamma_\infty under canonical rescaling. These results explain regulator dependence, finite predictivity, and the appearance of nonlocal form factors in ongoing asymptotic safety studies as consequences of projecting an underlying UV endpoint, rather than as fundamental features of the full theory. All statements are slab-local and admissibility-conditioned.
